title: Describing things
goal: Describe people and things by colour, size and quality, and compare them (bigger, the biggest).
intro:
Adjectives bring your Hindi to life. You'll learn the main colours and the most useful describing words, plus how to compare things.

The key grammar idea: adjectives ending in **-ā** change their ending to match the noun (अच्छा लड़का, अच्छी लड़की, अच्छे लड़के), while other adjectives never change. Comparison is easy — no '-er' or '-est', just **से** 'than' and **सबसे** 'than all'.

vocab.note: Calling someone मोटा is blunt but common in families.
For people use बूढ़ा or बड़ा.
बुरी, बुरे · also ख़राब xarāb 'bad, broken, spoilt' (invariable, very common)
invariable · तेज़ चाय 'strong tea', तेज़ बुख़ार 'high fever'

grammar.title: Adjective agreement
grammar.body:
Adjectives go **before** the noun, as in English. Adjectives ending in **-ā** (marked in this course with their -ī/-e forms) agree with the noun in gender, number and case:

**-ā** — masculine singular: अच्छा लड़का
**-e** — masculine plural, and masculine before a postposition (oblique): अच्छे लड़के; अच्छे लड़के को
**-ī** — all feminine: अच्छी लड़की, अच्छी लड़कियाँ

This includes the possessives (मेरा/मेरी/मेरे), का/की/के and ordinals — you already know the pattern!

All other adjectives are **invariable**: लाल, सफ़ेद, सुंदर, साफ़, भारी, गर्म, आसान: सुंदर लड़का, सुंदर लड़की.

The same agreement happens after 'to be': लड़का **लंबा** है, लड़की **लंबी** है, लड़के **लंबे** हैं.

examples.en: a white house and a white car (no change)

grammar.title: Comparing: से, ज़्यादा, सबसे
grammar.body:
Hindi has no '-er' ending. To say 'A is bigger than B', say **A B से बड़ा है** — 'A from B big is'. The adjective still agrees with A.

For emphasis add **ज़्यादा** 'more' or **कम** 'less': A B से **ज़्यादा** महँगा है 'A is more expensive than B'.

For 'the most / -est', use **सबसे** 'than all': **सबसे बड़ा** 'the biggest', **सबसे अच्छी** 'the best (f)'.

With pronouns, से joins on: मुझसे 'than me', तुमसे, आपसे, उससे, हमसे, उनसे.

Intensifiers: **बहुत** 'very', **काफ़ी** 'quite', **थोड़ा** 'a bit', **ज़्यादा** 'too': यह ज़्यादा गर्म है 'it's too hot'.

examples.en: Delhi is bigger than Jaipur. (दिल्ली is treated as feminine)
My brother is younger than me.

examples.native: यह किताब उससे ज़्यादा आसान है।
examples.roman: yah kitāb usse zyādā āsān hai.
examples.en: This book is easier than that one.
This is the most beautiful colour.

dialogue.title: The lost suitcase
dialogue.setting: Lisa's suitcase hasn't arrived at Delhi airport. She describes it at the baggage desk.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.en: What does your bag look like?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.native: बड़ा है, और काले रंग का है।
lines.roman: baṛā hai, aur kāle raṅg kā hai.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.native: नहीं, यह बहुत छोटा है। मेरा बैग इससे बड़ा और भारी है।
lines.roman: nahīṃ, yah bahut chhoṭā hai. merā baig isse baṛā aur bhārī hai.
lines.en: No, this one is too small. My bag is bigger and heavier than this.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.native: हाँ, उस पर एक लाल और पीला रिबन है।
lines.roman: hāṃ, us par ek lāl aur pīlā riban hai.
lines.en: Yes, there's a red and yellow ribbon on it.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.native: अच्छा… यह देखिए। काला, बड़ा, लाल-पीले रिबन वाला।
lines.roman: achchhā… yah dekhiye. kālā, baṛā, lāl-pīle riban vālā.
lines.en: Right… look at this. Black, big, with a red-and-yellow ribbon.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: Yes, that's it! Thank you so much!

culture: Colours carry strong meanings in India: **red** (लाल) is the colour of brides and celebration, **white** (सफ़ेद) is traditionally worn at funerals and by widows, **saffron** (केसरिया) is sacred, and **green** (हरा) is associated with Islam and prosperity. At Holi, everyone gets covered in every colour. Comments on appearance (मोटा, पतला, लंबा, or skin colour) are more direct than in many Western cultures — usually meant without malice, though attitudes are changing. The handy **वाला** turns anything into 'the one': नीला वाला 'the blue one', लाल रिबन वाला 'the one with the red ribbon'.
